## [Bugfix][Spec Decode] Clamp token_indices_to_sample to the request's first query row

Fixes #60897

## Purpose

`eagle_prepare_inputs_padded_kernel` (vllm/v1/spec_decode/utils.py) computes
`index_to_sample = q_last_tok_idx - num_rejected_tokens` without a lower
bound. When a request's query carries fewer rows than the rejection count
assumes, the index underflows past the start of the request:

- For the first request, the index is negative → out-of-bounds gather.
- For any later request, the index lands inside the **previous request's**
  rows → silently cross-wired sampled tokens and corrupted drafting.

The underflow is reachable when the query has no bonus-token row. With
PP > 1, the scheduler can schedule only the draft tokens
(`num_scheduled_tokens == num_draft_tokens`), while
`valid_sampled_tokens_count` still assumes the bonus row is present
(`num_rejected_tokens = num_draft_tokens + 1 - valid_count`). The same
unclamped formula exists in the CPU implementation
(csrc/cpu/spec_decode_utils.cpp), so both backends are affected.

Downstream, `token_indices_to_sample` is consumed by
`drafter.propose(...)` to select per-request sampled tokens
(vllm/v1/worker/gpu_model_runner.py), so an out-of-range index corrupts
every subsequent decode step.

## Reproducer

Unit-level, hermetic (no network, no gated models). Runs on any CUDA GPU
(e.g., an RTX 3090 24GB) — the kernel is pure integer index arithmetic, so
the bug is hardware-independent:

```bash
python -m pytest tests/v1/spec_decode/test_eagle.py::test_prepare_inputs_padded_index_stays_within_request_rows -x -q
```

Two requests, 2 draft tokens each, query contains only the draft tokens
(no bonus row), entire draft rejected (`valid_sampled_tokens_count = [1, 1]`).

Before the fix, the kernel emits `[-1, 1]` — request 1 gathers out of
bounds, request 2 gathers request 1's rows [evidence: before.log].
After the fix, `[0, 2]` — both clamped to their own first query row
[evidence: after.log].

## Fix

Clamp `index_to_sample` to `query_start_loc[req_idx]` (the request's own
first row) in both implementations:

- Triton kernel: `tl.maximum(index_to_sample, tl.load(query_start_loc_gpu_ptr + req_idx))`
- CPU C++: `std::max(index_to_sample, query_loc_ptr[req_idx])`

This is a no-op whenever the bonus row is present: with
`valid_count >= 1`, `num_rejected_tokens <= num_draft_tokens` and the raw
index is already `>= query_start_loc[req_idx]`. The boundary is exercised
by a test where a fully-rejected request lands exactly on its first row
[evidence: normal-path.log].

Clamping to the request's own start (rather than to 0) is required for
multi-request batches: `index_to_sample` is an absolute row index, so a
0-clamp would point later requests into request 1's rows.

## Test plan

```bash
python -m pytest tests/v1/spec_decode/test_eagle.py -k prepare_inputs_padded -q
```

Two new tests in tests/v1/spec_decode/test_eagle.py (hermetic configs, no
network):

- `test_prepare_inputs_padded_index_stays_within_request_rows` — the
  underflow scenario above; asserts `[0, 2]`.
- `test_prepare_inputs_padded_unaffected_when_bonus_row_present` — the
  standard layout (bonus row present, rejections `[1, 0, 2]`); asserts the
  historical expected output `[1, 5, 6]`, proving the clamp is a no-op
  including the exact-boundary case.

The pre-existing `test_prepare_inputs_padded` (same scenario via gated
meta-llama configs) runs in upstream CI.

## Test results

- Before fix: `AssertionError ... tensor([-1, 1], device='cuda:0') != tensor([0, 2])` [evidence: before.log]
- After fix: `1 passed` [evidence: after.log]
- Normal path (bonus row present): `2 passed` (both new tests; the
  pre-existing gated-config test cannot run locally for lack of
  meta-llama access — environment limitation, not code) [evidence: normal-path.log]

## Duplicate work check

Searched open issues and PRs for: `token_indices_to_sample`,
`eagle_prepare_inputs_padded`, `num_rejected_tokens underflow`,
`spec decode PP index`. No open issue or PR addresses this underflow.
The kernel was introduced in #28597 / #24539 (merged 2025); the unclamped
formula is unchanged since.

## AI assistance

AI assistance (opencode) was used to trace the root cause, implement the
clamp in both backends, and prepare this PR. The human submitter reviewed
every changed line and ran the validation on a CUDA GPU.

Co-authored-by: opencode <noreply@opencode.ai>
Signed-off-by: michael-gpu <18089103+michael-gpu@users.noreply.github.com>

🚀

First-time contributor. Fixes a spec-decode index underflow under PP > 1 (#60897) — a 3-line clamp in both the Triton and CPU implementations, with a hermetic reproducer and before/after evidence in the description. I've reviewed every line and validated on hardware. Could a maintainer add the ready label so CI can run? Thanks.

Independently walked the arithmetic on current main and it checks out. With the bonus row present, query_len = num_draft + 1 and valid_count >= 1, so num_rejected <= num_draft = query_len - 1 and the clamp never engages; the no-op test pins exactly that. Without the bonus row (query_len == num_draft) a fully rejected draft gives num_rejected == num_draft and index_to_sample lands on query_start_loc - 1: -1 for the first request, the previous request's last row for the rest. The [-1, 1] example from the issue falls out of the formula exactly.

Both call sites are covered: the Triton kernel here and the CPU twin (csrc/cpu/spec_decode_utils.cpp had the same unclamped line). query_start_loc[req_idx] is the right clamp boundary, it keeps the gather inside the request's own rows in every case.

One premise I cannot confirm from source alone: that PP actually produces num_scheduled_tokens == num_draft_tokens (no bonus row) in the wild. The kernel bug is real given the input state, and the clamp is harmless when the state never occurs, so this is worth taking either way. If someone with a PP setup can point at the draft-only scheduling step, that closes the loop.

Thanks for the independent verification — and for pushing on the premise; it led to a stronger answer than the PR originally carried.

**On the PP premise:** the draft-only scheduling state is real — we hit it in production with PP + MTP (async scheduling disabled): the worker-side sanity assert fired with 1 query row vs 2 logits rows, which is exactly the no-bonus-row state reaching the spec-decode path. On current main that state trips the assert at `vllm/v1/worker/gpu/model_runner.py` (`assert (num_scheduled_tokens_np >= num_logits).all()` — its comment acknowledges query rows can come up short) rather than reaching the kernel, so on main it manifests as a crash, not silent corruption.

**But the underflow is reachable on current main without PP**, via the drafter's discard path: `eagle_prepare_next_token_padded_kernel` (vllm/v1/spec_decode/utils.py) stores `valid_sampled_tokens_count = 0` for requests the drafter discarded (over capacity). `num_rejected_tokens` then evaluates to `num_draft + 1` while the query still carries the bonus row, so `index_to_sample = query_start_loc[req] - 2` — with the scheduler's assert still satisfied. I've added a third test covering exactly this input state (`test_prepare_inputs_padded_discarded_request_zero_valid_count`): before the fix the kernel emits `[-1, 2]`, after the fix `[0, 3]`, captured on an RTX 3090 (before/after logs in the description).

The clamp stands either way, as you said — but the discard path makes it a live correctness fix on main, not just hardening.

That closes the loop nicely. The production assert firing with 1 query row against 2 logits rows is exactly the state I could not confirm from source alone, and the discard path is a better catch than the PP route: valid_sampled_tokens_count=0 with the bonus row still present reaches the underflow with the scheduler assert satisfied, so it is live on current main with no exotic topology. The new test pinning [-1, 2] to [0, 3] on real hardware is the right evidence shape.

From my side the verification chain is complete: two independent reachability paths, arithmetic checked against current main, clamp behavior neutral in the no-underflow case. Good luck with the maintainer pass.

## Claude Code Review

This pull request is from a fork — automated review is disabled. A repository maintainer can comment `@claude review` to run a one-time review.

 from typing import Literal
 from unittest import mock
 
@@ -352,6 +354,201 @@ def test_prepare_inputs_padded():
     assert torch.equal(token_indices_to_sample, expected_token_indices_to_sample)
 
 
+def test_prepare_inputs_padded_index_stays_within_request_rows(tmp_path, monkeypatch):
+    """token_indices_to_sample must stay within each request's own query rows.
+
+    Regression: when a request's query carries no bonus-token row (observed
+    with PP > 1, where the scheduler can schedule only the draft tokens),
+    q_last_tok_idx - num_rejected_tokens underflows past the start of the
+    request. For the first request this yields -1 (out-of-bounds gather);
+    for later requests it yields an index inside the previous request's
+    rows, silently cross-wiring their sampled tokens.
+    """
+    device = torch.device(DEVICE_TYPE)
+
+    # Hermetic configs: prepare_inputs_padded is pure metadata math and
+    # never loads weights, so minimal local configs avoid network and
+    # gated-repo dependencies.
+    config = {
+        "architectures": ["LlamaForCausalLM"],
+        "model_type": "llama",
+        "hidden_size": 64,
+        "intermediate_size": 128,
+        "num_attention_heads": 4,
+        "num_key_value_heads": 4,
+        "num_hidden_layers": 1,
+        "vocab_size": 128,
+        "max_position_embeddings": 512,
+    }
+    for name in ("target", "draft"):
+        model_path = tmp_path / name
+        model_path.mkdir()
+        (model_path / "config.json").write_text(json.dumps(config))
+    monkeypatch.setattr(sys.modules[__name__], "model_dir", str(tmp_path / "target"))
+    monkeypatch.setattr(sys.modules[__name__], "eagle_dir", str(tmp_path / "draft"))
+
+    # Two requests, 2 draft tokens each, query contains ONLY the draft
+    # tokens (no bonus row): query_start_loc = [0, 2, 4].
+    batch_spec = BatchSpec(
+        seq_lens=[8, 8],
+        query_lens=[2, 2],
+    )
+    common_attn_metadata = create_common_attn_metadata(
+        batch_spec,
+        block_size=BLOCK_SIZE,
+        device=device,
+    )
+    spec_decode_metadata = SpecDecodeMetadata.make_dummy(
+        draft_token_ids=[[0, 0], [0, 0]],
+        device=device,
+    )
+    # Entire draft rejected: valid_count = 0 accepted + 1 bonus.
+    valid_sampled_tokens_count = torch.tensor([1, 1], dtype=torch.int32, device=device)
+
+    proposer = _create_proposer("eagle", 2)
+
+    _, token_indices_to_sample, num_rejected_tokens_gpu = (
+        proposer.prepare_inputs_padded(
+            common_attn_metadata, spec_decode_metadata, valid_sampled_tokens_count
+        )
+    )
+
+    expected_num_rejected = torch.tensor([2, 2], dtype=torch.int32, device=device)
+    assert torch.equal(num_rejected_tokens_gpu, expected_num_rejected)
+
+    # Before the fix this was [-1, 1]: request 1 underflows to -1 and
+    # request 2 lands inside request 1's rows. Both must clamp to their
+    # own first query row.
+    expected_indices = torch.tensor([0, 2], dtype=torch.int32, device=device)
+    assert torch.equal(token_indices_to_sample, expected_indices)
+
+
+def test_prepare_inputs_padded_discarded_request_zero_valid_count(
+    tmp_path, monkeypatch
+):
+    """A discarded request (valid_count == 0) underflows by two rows.
+
+    eagle_prepare_next_token_padded_kernel stores valid_count = 0 for
+    requests the drafter discarded (over capacity). num_rejected then
+    evaluates to num_draft + 1 while the query still carries the bonus
+    row, so index_to_sample = query_start_loc[req] - 2 before the fix —
+    with the scheduler's own sanity assert
+    (num_scheduled >= num_draft + num_bonus) still satisfied. Reachable
+    on current main without pipeline parallelism.
+    """
+    device = torch.device(DEVICE_TYPE)
+
+    config = {
+        "architectures": ["LlamaForCausalLM"],
+        "model_type": "llama",
+        "hidden_size": 64,
+        "intermediate_size": 128,
+        "num_attention_heads": 4,
+        "num_key_value_heads": 4,
+        "num_hidden_layers": 1,
+        "vocab_size": 128,
+        "max_position_embeddings": 512,
+    }
+    for name in ("target", "draft"):
+        model_path = tmp_path / name
+        model_path.mkdir()
+        (model_path / "config.json").write_text(json.dumps(config))
+    monkeypatch.setattr(sys.modules[__name__], "model_dir", str(tmp_path / "target"))
+    monkeypatch.setattr(sys.modules[__name__], "eagle_dir", str(tmp_path / "draft"))
+
+    # Standard layout (bonus row present): query = 2 drafts + 1 bonus row.
+    batch_spec = BatchSpec(
+        seq_lens=[8, 8],
+        query_lens=[3, 3],
+    )
+    common_attn_metadata = create_common_attn_metadata(
+        batch_spec,
+        block_size=BLOCK_SIZE,
+        device=device,
+    )
+    spec_decode_metadata = SpecDecodeMetadata.make_dummy(
+        draft_token_ids=[[0, 0], [0, 0]],
+        device=device,
+    )
+    # Both requests discarded by the drafter: valid_count = 0.
+    valid_sampled_tokens_count = torch.tensor(
+        [0, 0], dtype=torch.int32, device=device
+    )
+
+    proposer = _create_proposer("eagle", 2)
+
+    _, token_indices_to_sample, num_rejected_tokens_gpu = (
+        proposer.prepare_inputs_padded(
+            common_attn_metadata, spec_decode_metadata, valid_sampled_tokens_count
+        )
+    )
+
+    # num_rejected = 2 + 1 - 0 = 3 for both requests.
+    expected_num_rejected = torch.tensor([3, 3], dtype=torch.int32, device=device)
+    assert torch.equal(num_rejected_tokens_gpu, expected_num_rejected)
+
+    # Before the fix: [-1, 2] — request 1 gathers out of bounds, request 2
+    # lands on request 1's last row. Both must clamp to their own first row.
+    expected_indices = torch.tensor([0, 3], dtype=torch.int32, device=device)
+    assert torch.equal(token_indices_to_sample, expected_indices)
+
+
+def test_prepare_inputs_padded_unaffected_when_bonus_row_present(tmp_path, monkeypatch):
+    """The clamp is a no-op on the standard path (bonus token in query)."""
+    device = torch.device(DEVICE_TYPE)
+
+    config = {
+        "architectures": ["LlamaForCausalLM"],
+        "model_type": "llama",
+        "hidden_size": 64,
+        "intermediate_size": 128,
+        "num_attention_heads": 4,
+        "num_key_value_heads": 4,
+        "num_hidden_layers": 1,
+        "vocab_size": 128,
+        "max_position_embeddings": 512,
+    }
+    for name in ("target", "draft"):
+        model_path = tmp_path / name
+        model_path.mkdir()
+        (model_path / "config.json").write_text(json.dumps(config))
+    monkeypatch.setattr(sys.modules[__name__], "model_dir", str(tmp_path / "target"))
+    monkeypatch.setattr(sys.modules[__name__], "eagle_dir", str(tmp_path / "draft"))
+
+    # Standard layout: query = 2 draft tokens + 1 bonus row per request.
+    # Rejections [1, 0, 2] put request 3 exactly at its first row (index 6
+    # == query_start_loc[2]), exercising the clamp boundary from above.
+    batch_spec = BatchSpec(
+        seq_lens=[3, 3, 3],
+        query_lens=[3, 3, 3],
+    )
+    common_attn_metadata = create_common_attn_metadata(
+        batch_spec,
+        block_size=BLOCK_SIZE,
+        device=device,
+    )
+    spec_decode_metadata = SpecDecodeMetadata.make_dummy(
+        draft_token_ids=[[0, 0]] * 3,
+        device=device,
+    )
+    valid_sampled_tokens_count = torch.tensor(
+        [2, 3, 1], dtype=torch.int32, device=device
+    )
+
+    proposer = _create_proposer("eagle", 2)
+
+    _, token_indices_to_sample, num_rejected_tokens_gpu = (
+        proposer.prepare_inputs_padded(
+            common_attn_metadata, spec_decode_metadata, valid_sampled_tokens_count
+        )
+    )
+
+    expected_num_rejected = torch.tensor([1, 0, 2], dtype=torch.int32, device=device)
+    assert torch.equal(num_rejected_tokens_gpu, expected_num_rejected)
+    expected_indices = torch.tensor([1, 5, 6], dtype=torch.int32, device=device)
+    assert torch.equal(token_indices_to_sample, expected_indices)
+
+
 def test_set_inputs_first_pass_default_eagle():
     """Test for set_inputs_first_pass without extra input slots (default EAGLE).

@@ -224,6 +224,13 @@ def eagle_prepare_inputs_padded_kernel(
     q_last_tok_idx = tl.load(query_start_loc_gpu_ptr + req_idx + 1) - 1
 
     index_to_sample = q_last_tok_idx - num_rejected_tokens
+    # The query may carry fewer rows than num_rejected_tokens assumes (e.g.
+    # with PP > 1 the scheduler can schedule only the draft tokens, without

+    index_to_sample = tl.maximum(
+        index_to_sample, tl.load(query_start_loc_gpu_ptr + req_idx)

Without the bonus row (query_len == num_draft) a fully rejected draft gives num_rejected == num_draft and index_to_sample lands on query_start_loc - 1: -1 for the first request, the previous request's last row for the rest. The [-1, 1] example from the issue falls out of the formula exactly.

Both call sites are covered: the Triton kernel here and the CPU twin (csrc/cpu/spec_decode_utils.cpp had the same unclamped line). query_start_loc[req_idx] is the right clamp boundary, it keeps the gather inside the request's own rows in every case.

One premise I cannot confirm from source alone: that PP actually produces num_scheduled_tokens == num_draft_tokens (no bonus row) in the wild. The kernel bug is real given the input state, and the clamp is harmless when the state never occurs, so this is worth taking either way. If someone with a PP setup can point at the draft-only scheduling step, that closes the loop.

Thanks for the independent verification — and for pushing on the premise; it led to a stronger answer than the PR originally carried.

**On the PP premise:** the draft-only scheduling state is real — we hit it in production with PP + MTP (async scheduling disabled): the worker-side sanity assert fired with 1 query row vs 2 logits rows, which is exactly the no-bonus-row state reaching the spec-decode path. On current main that state trips the assert at `vllm/v1/worker/gpu/model_runner.py` (`assert (num_scheduled_tokens_np >= num_logits).all()` — its comment acknowledges query rows can come up short) rather than reaching the kernel, so on main it manifests as a crash, not silent corruption.

**But the underflow is reachable on current main without PP**, via the drafter's discard path: `eagle_prepare_next_token_padded_kernel` (vllm/v1/spec_decode/utils.py) stores `valid_sampled_tokens_count = 0` for requests the drafter discarded (over capacity). `num_rejected_tokens` then evaluates to `num_draft + 1` while the query still carries the bonus row, so `index_to_sample = query_start_loc[req] - 2` — with the scheduler's assert still satisfied. I've added a third test covering exactly this input state (`test_prepare_inputs_padded_discarded_request_zero_valid_count`): before the fix the kernel emits `[-1, 2]`, after the fix `[0, 3]`, captured on an RTX 3090 (before/after logs in the description).

The clamp stands either way, as you said — but the discard path makes it a live correctness fix on main, not just hardening.

That closes the loop nicely. The production assert firing with 1 query row against 2 logits rows is exactly the state I could not confirm from source alone, and the discard path is a better catch than the PP route: valid_sampled_tokens_count=0 with the bonus row still present reaches the underflow with the scheduler assert satisfied, so it is live on current main with no exotic topology. The new test pinning [-1, 2] to [0, 3] on real hardware is the right evidence shape.

From my side the verification chain is complete: two independent reachability paths, arithmetic checked against current main, clamp behavior neutral in the no-underflow case. Good luck with the maintainer pass.
